title: Binomial pricing and American exercise

objectives.text: Derive two-state risk-neutral weights from replication/no-arbitrage and compute bounded European backward induction under explicit no-dividend per-period gross-return assumptions.
Compare continuation with intrinsic payoff at each allowed exercise node,distinguishing finite-grid American-style approximation,European rights and real-world probability/model limits.
Build the public CRR factors and exercise-enabled put recurrence at N<=1000 while preserving grid, probability, units and in-place update invariants.

blocks.markdown: One stock starts at S>0. Each period multiplies by fixed uor d,with0<d<a<u,where a>0is the risk-free money-market GROSS return per period. There are no dividends,fees,bid-ask spread,taxes,default,position constraints or borrowing/lending rate differences;fractional stock and borrowing/shorting needed for replication are allowed. Rates and factors are deterministic and identical across nodes. These are model assumptions,not descriptions of all markets. With annual continuous rate r and period length hyears,a=exp(r*h);a simple per-period rate Rwould instead mean a=1+R.

For one-period payoff V_u,V_d,choose stock holding Delta=(V_u-V_d)/(S*(u-d))and initial money-market amount B=(u*V_d-d*V_u)/(a*(u-d)). Then Delta*S*u+B*a=V_uand Delta*S*d+B*a=V_d. Under the model's no-arbitrage replication argument,the initial claim value is Delta*S+B. Rearranging gives V=((1-p)*V_d+p*V_u)/a,with p=(a-d)/(u-d). Strict d<a<uensures0<p<1. Do not clip invalid pinto[0,1]and silently claim a valid tree.

blocks.title: A pricing weight is not the physical up chance

American exercise means the contractual right to exercise before expiration;European exercise is at expiration. Our finite model permits exercise only at the listed tree dates,so it is a finite-grid approximation to continuously available American exercise,or an exact model of those discrete opportunities. American-enabled value is at least European under identical model inputs because holding remains an available choice. Do not generalize a no-dividend,nonnegative-rate call no-early-exercise result to dividends,negative rates,frictions or different settlement contracts. This lesson uses the actual maxcomparison instead of an unconditional shortcut.

The risk-neutral weight makes p*u+(1-p)*d=a. It prices replicable claims under the stated frictionless model without using the stock's physical expected return. It is not an estimate of profit chance,and no-arbitrage within two states does not prove the real market follows those states or that execution permits the hedge. Negative per-period interest corresponds to0<a<1and is admitted when strict d<a<ustill holds. Do not replace that with an assumption a>=1unless the theorem or interface explicitly requires it.

The code stores one level,then builds a NEW previous-level vector,so updating one node cannot overwrite a child still needed by another. It visits O(n^2)nodes with O(n)stored values;exact rational numerator/denominator bit costs can grow with n,so these are node-count bounds,not constant-time arithmetic promises. Exponentiation uses exact positive factors. Steps<=16and input bounds limit teaching work,but arbitrary tiny Fraction denominators are not a hostile-input resource budget. A deployed service would need payload/bit-size limits and runtime controls separately.

Extend the exact toy model with a declared CRR grid

The earlier price_tree accepts exact rational factors and steps<=16. This practice function instead receives S,K,r,sigma,T,N with ordinary floats and N<=1000. Use dt=T/N, u=exp(sigma*sqrt(dt)), d=1/u, growth=exp(r*dt), q=(growth-d)/(u-d), discount=exp(-r*dt). Annual r is continuous decimal rate, sigma is annualized decimal volatility and T is years. The guaranteed 0<q<1 is the no-arbitrage interval; it is not an estimated physical up probability. Do not clamp a bad q into range or silently broaden the old helper.

One row of values and a safe overwrite direction

At maturity j up moves give stock S*u^j*d^(N-j) and payoff max(K-stock,0). At level i,j, continuation=discount*(q*next[j+1]+(1-q)*next[j]); value=max(0,K-node_stock,continuation). The code rewrites j in INCREASING order: when writing values[j], both old children values[j] and values[j+1] are still available. Decreasing order would read an overwritten up-child. Entries beyond the new row length are ignored. This is exercise at tree dates, not a continuous-time early-exercise solver.

Compute node stocks without multiplying competing huge powers

Because d=1/u mathematically, node stock can be evaluated as S*exp((2*j-i)*sigma*sqrt(dt)). This avoids separately computing u^j and d^(i-j), whose intermediate factors can overflow even when their product is finite. The public bounds give maximum absolute node log-factor sigma*sqrt(T*N)<=100, so exp is finite here. This is algebraically the same tree with an explicit floating evaluation choice, not a claim of bitwise equality to every power library. Tests must compare the displayed answer against an independent higher-precision tree away from stated ties.

Trace, cost and rights

S=K=100,r=.05,sigma=.2,T=1,N=3 gives6.499560. At every node the holder can keep the option, so its value is at least the immediate put payoff and at least the otherwise identical European tree. O(N^2) node work and O(N) value memory meet N<=1000; there is no exponential path enumeration in this implementation. Test one-step exercise versus continuation, deep in/out of money, zero rate, near-edge valid q and maximum N. Increasing N need not make successive grid prices monotone. Grid convergence and market model fit are different questions; no account exercise/trading action follows.

blocks.source:
from collections import OrderedDict, deque
from bisect import bisect_left
import heapq
import math
from fractions import Fraction

def american_put(S, K, r, sigma, T, N):
    dt = T / N
    log_up = sigma * math.sqrt(dt)
    up = math.exp(log_up)
    down = 1 / up
    q = (math.exp(r * dt) - down) / (up - down)
    discount = math.exp(-r * dt)
    values = [max(K - S * math.exp((2 * j - N) * log_up), 0.0) for j in range(N + 1)]
    for level in range(N - 1, -1, -1):
        for j in range(level + 1):
            continuation = discount * (q * values[j + 1] + (1 - q) * values[j])
            intrinsic = K - S * math.exp((2 * j - level) * log_up)
            values[j] = max(0.0, intrinsic, continuation)
    return [f'{values[0]:.6f}']

print(*american_put(100.0,100.0,.05,.2,1.0,3))
